correctness.rationale: The actual signed-antichain representation gives the join of two standard coordinate cubes; its support is the maximum of two independent half-normal sums. Symmetry of Gaussian signs gives exact per-vertex probabilities and the order-two collision expression. The full-domain finite half-normal mgf enables the triangular-array Cramér rate for the rare smaller-block exposure. The rate is strictly convex as a function of block proportion by an explicit envelope second derivative, and its crossing with a linear entropy cost is uniquely interior. The exact p=2,q=1 orthant check agrees with an independently integrated half-normal convolution. Packaged CHECK.py passed 1600 direct support-function comparisons and all stated numerical tests; asymptotic proof is analytical and does not rely on tests.

value.rationale: This is a natural collision invariant of Gaussian normal cones for an infinite, classically motivated family of enriched-chain/Hanner polytopes. Two competing vertex orbit sizes and exposure masses yield an unexpected effect: an exponentially rare orbit controls two-direction collisions over a nontrivial open range of macroscopic imbalance. The work proves a complete sharp phase classification, including a unique critical proportion; it is neither a small parameter improvement nor a bare finite table. Exact low-dimensional angular benchmarks make the invariant concrete.
